docs.text: UltraGPS Ground Station ¶ Ground control program for the St. Mary's University UltraGPS positioning system, developed as a result of graduate research. UltraGpsXY is designed to run on the ground-station host, which is the computer that is connected to the base-station Arduino + UltraGPS shield combo through USB. It maintains a serial link to the base-station and allows commands to be sent to the base-station from the network through a TCP command socket and a UDP data stream. This allows other computers, from within the same network, to communicate to the base-station without having to be physically connected to the base-station. This program must be running in order for the UltraGPSControl program to properly. Documentation ¶ Architecture — how the program is structured and how data flows between the Arduino, the modules, and network clients. Installation — building from source or installing the Debian package. Usage — running the program and its command-line options. At a glance ¶ Binary UltraGpsXY Language C++17 (CMake) Serial default /dev/ttyACM0 @ 38400 bps Default TCP command port 9000 Default UDP stream port 9001 Platform Linux (packaged for Ubuntu/Debian, amd64)

docs.text: Architecture ¶ UltraGpsXY is a single C++17 executable built with CMake. It is organised around a main.cpp control loop and three modules, plus three third-party libraries that are compiled in statically. Components ¶ Component Location Responsibility Control loop main.cpp Argument parsing, module setup, banner, main event loop Comms module CommsModule/ Command validation and framing over the serial link Serial module SerialModule/ Low-level POSIX serial (termios) I/O to the Arduino Server module ServerModule/ TCP command socket + UDP continuous data stream Third-party libraries ¶ These are vendored as git submodules and statically linked , so the shipped binary has no third-party runtime dependencies: spdlog — logging. tomlplusplus — TOML parsing. argparse — command-line parsing. Data flow ¶ Base-station Arduino │ (USB serial, e.g. /dev/ttyACM0 @ 38400) ▼ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ SerialModule │◄──────►│ CommsModule │ └──────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌───────▼────────┐ │ main() loop │ └───────┬────────┘ │ ┌───────▼────────┐ │ ServerModule │ └───────┬────────┘ TCP commands (9000) │ UDP stream (9001) ▼ Network clients Control loop ¶ The loop in main() runs continuously and, on each pass: Receives TCP commands from network clients via the Server module. Validates each command through the Comms module, discarding anything invalid. Dispatches by command type: Normal commands are sent to the Arduino and the response is returned to the requesting client over TCP. Continuous commands switch the system into streaming mode. Streams data : while in continuous mode, serial data from the Arduino is pushed out to clients over UDP. Logging ¶ Logging uses spdlog . The SPDLOG_* macros are gated at compile time by SPDLOG_ACTIVE_LEVEL : Default build — the macros are compiled out entirely. Direct calls such as spdlog::info() (banner, module-init messages) are always present, regardless of compilation debug level. -DVERBOSE_LOGGING=ON — all SPDLOG_* macros are active at DEBUG level and the build switches to a debug configuration. See Installation and Usage .

docs.text: Developer's Guide ¶ A self-contained reference for developers who fork the repository and need to work with the project's tooling — building, packaging, previewing the documentation, and cutting releases. Everything needed is on this page. Overview ¶ UltraGpsXY is a single C++17 executable that runs on the ground-station host and bridges the positioning hardware to the network: Maintains a serial link to the base-station Arduino (default /dev/ttyACM0 @ 38400 bps) via the Comms/Serial modules. Runs a TCP command server (default port 9000 ): network clients send commands, which are validated and forwarded to the Arduino, and the response is returned to the client. Runs a UDP data stream (default port 9001 ): while in continuous mode, live position data from the Arduino is streamed out to clients. The third-party libraries ( spdlog , tomlplusplus , argparse ) are vendored as git submodules and statically linked, so the installed binary has no third-party runtime dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++17 compiler (GCC or Clang) and CMake ≥ 3.15 git (the third-party libraries are git submodules) dpkg / cpack — only needed to build the .deb package Python 3 with pip — only needed to build/preview the documentation Clone with submodules: git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Imperious22M/UltraGPS-Ground.git cd UltraGPS-Ground # If you already cloned without --recurse-submodules: git submodule update --init --recursive Installing a prebuilt release ¶ You don't need to build anything to run the program — each release ships a prebuilt Debian package. Download the latest .deb from the Releases page and install it: sudo dpkg -i ultragps-xy_*_amd64.deb This installs UltraGpsXY to /usr/bin (on your PATH ) and pulls in its runtime dependencies automatically. Using the build script ¶ build.sh is the single entry point for building, packaging, cleaning, and previewing the docs. Run it from the repository root: ./build.sh <command> [options] Commands ¶ Command What it does build Compile the UltraGpsXY binary into ./build/ deb Build the installable Debian package into ./build/ clean Remove the ./build/ directory (like make clean ) docs Preview the documentation locally with live reload docs-build Render the static documentation site into ./site/ Options ¶ Option Applies to Effect -v , --verbose build Configure with -DVERBOSE_LOGGING=ON (debug build, SPDLOG_* macros active) -h , --help — Show usage Compiling the program ¶ ./build.sh build # optimised binary → ./build/UltraGpsXY ./build.sh build --verbose # debug build with verbose logging compiled in Run it: ./build/UltraGpsXY # or just `UltraGpsXY` if installed via the .deb Common options (see the Usage page or UltraGpsXY --help for the full list): ./build/UltraGpsXY --serial-port /dev/ttyUSB0 --baud-rate 115200 ./build/UltraGpsXY --net-device eth0 --tcp-port 9100 --udp-port 9101 --verbose Building and installing the Debian package ¶ ./build.sh deb # → ./build/ultragps-xy_<version>_amd64.deb sudo dpkg -i build/ultragps-xy_*_amd64.deb This installs the binary to /usr/bin/UltraGpsXY (on your PATH ) and resolves its runtime dependencies ( libc6 , libstdc++6 , libgcc-s1 ) automatically. Note The deb target builds in a temporary directory under /tmp rather than in place, then copies the finished .deb into ./build/ . This isolates the transient files dpkg-shlibdeps creates while packaging from the working tree; plain compilation is unaffected. Cleaning ¶ ./build.sh clean # removes ./build/ Previewing the documentation ¶ The docs are built with MkDocs . To preview them locally without pushing: pip install -r docs/requirements.txt # one-time: install MkDocs ./build.sh docs # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000 ./build.sh docs-build # render static site into ./site/ Pushing documentation changes to the release branch automatically rebuilds and republishes the site via GitHub Actions. Releasing a version ¶ Released versions live in the repository's Releases tab, each with the .deb package attached. The release branch is the stable snapshot of the most recent release. Releases are cut by pushing a version tag ( vX.Y ). Pushing the tag triggers the Release workflow, which builds the .deb and publishes a GitHub Release with it attached. To cut a release: Bump the version in CMakeLists.txt so it matches the tag you intend to push — project(UltraGpsXY VERSION X.Y ...) . The release workflow fails if the tag and the package version disagree, so this must be done first. Push that commit onto the release branch: git checkout release git merge --ff-only <your-dev-branch> git push origin release Tag the release commit and push the tag: git tag vX.Y # e.g. v1.0 — must match project(VERSION) above git push origin vX.Y The workflow then builds ultragps-xy_X.Y_amd64.deb and attaches it to a new release named "UltraGPS Ground Station vX.Y", with auto-generated notes. Users can then download and install it: sudo dpkg -i ultragps-xy_X.Y_amd64.deb

docs.text: Installation ¶ There are two ways to get UltraGpsXY onto a machine: install the prebuilt Debian package from a release, or build it from source. Install from a release (recommended) ¶ Each tagged version is published on the Releases page with the .deb package attached. Download the latest ultragps-xy_<version>_amd64.deb and install it: sudo dpkg -i ultragps-xy_*_amd64.deb This installs the binary to /usr/bin/UltraGpsXY (on your PATH ) and pulls in its runtime dependencies ( libc6 , libstdc++6 , libgcc-s1 ) automatically. Prerequisites ¶ A C++17 compiler (GCC or Clang) and CMake ≥ 3.15 git (the third-party libraries are git submodules) Build from source ¶ Clone with submodules, then build with the helper script: git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Imperious22M/UltraGPS-Ground.git cd UltraGPS-Ground # If you already cloned without --recurse-submodules: git submodule update --init --recursive ./build.sh build # optimised binary → ./build/UltraGpsXY ./build.sh build --verbose # debug build with SPDLOG macros active ./build.sh clean removes the build/ directory (equivalent to make clean ). Building without the helper script build.sh just wraps CMake: cmake -S . -B build cmake --build build -j "$(nproc)" Debian package (.deb) ¶ Build a .deb with the helper script: ./build.sh deb # → ./build/ultragps-xy_<version>_amd64.deb Install it: sudo dpkg -i build/ultragps-xy_*_amd64.deb This installs the binary to /usr/bin/UltraGpsXY , so it lands on your PATH . Runtime dependencies ( libc6 , libstdc++6 , libgcc-s1 ) are resolved automatically by the package. Packaging builds in an isolated directory The deb target intentionally builds in a temporary directory under /tmp rather than in place, then copies the finished .deb into ./build/ . This isolates the transient files dpkg-shlibdeps creates while packaging from the working tree.

docs.text: Usage ¶ Run the program directly (if installed via the .deb , UltraGpsXY is on your PATH ; otherwise use ./build/UltraGpsXY ): UltraGpsXY [options] On startup it prints a banner summarising the resolved serial port, baud rate, IP address, and ports, then initialises the Comms module (serial link) and starts the Server module. Command-line options ¶ All configuration is done through flags — there is no configuration file read at runtime. Flag Argument Default Description -v , --verbose — off Enable verbose (debug-level) logging at runtime -s , --serial-port path /dev/ttyACM0 Serial port for the base-station Arduino -b , --baud-rate uint 38400 Baud rate; one of 9600 , 19200 , 38400 , 57600 , 115200 -n , --net-device name (auto) Network interface to bind for the server (default: active network) -t , --tcp-port uint 9000 TCP port for the command server -u , --udp-port uint 9001 UDP port for the continuous data stream -T , --server-timeout uint (ms) 5000 Server timeout in milliseconds Examples ¶ Run with defaults: UltraGpsXY Custom serial port and baud rate: UltraGpsXY --serial-port /dev/ttyUSB0 --baud-rate 115200 Bind the server to a specific interface and ports, with verbose logging: UltraGpsXY --net-device eth0 --tcp-port 9100 --udp-port 9101 --verbose Runtime verbose vs. compile-time verbose --verbose raises the runtime log level to debug for direct spdlog calls. The SPDLOG_* macros (fine-grained loop tracing) are separate and are only compiled in when the binary is built with -DVERBOSE_LOGGING=ON (see Installation ).
